text:
tariq: FYI saw a regression where a reclaimed prefix slot got reused while a slow reader was still traversing pointers. We get corrupted read semantics (not just stale), so I think we need a reclamation strategy, not just faster handoff protocols.

hao: ouch. Do you have a minimized repro?

tariq: yes, small harness that spins a long-running read (holds pointer into value) while we evict+recreate the prefix. The reader sees memory from the new tenant; sometimes it follows freed pointers.

nora: that sounds like a classic use-after-free. Generation tags avoid ABA but still allow in-place reuse if readers hold direct pointers. We need something that prevents physical reuse until all readers are done.

anya: agree. One approach is epoch-based reclamation (EBR): advance a global epoch periodically; readers announce epoch entry/exit; evict queues items tagged with epoch; only free when safe. Cheap per-read path if we do lightweight reader counters.

hao: sketch code?

nora: pseudo:
```
reader_enter() { r_epoch = global_epoch; reader_counters[core] = r_epoch; }
reader_exit() { reader_counters[core] = 0; }
evict(slot) { slot.del_epoch = global_epoch; retire_list.push(slot); }
reclaim_thread() {
  while(true) {
    min_epoch = min(reader_counters[])
    global_epoch++
    for s in retire_list: if s.del_epoch < min_epoch: free(s)
  }
}
```
This guarantees no reader is in an older epoch when free occurs.

tariq: pros: prevents UAF without per-object CAS on the hot path; cons: global_epoch coordination, need to handle stalled readers (long GC pauses), and impact on rolling restarts.

hao: rolling restarts are tricky. If a node dies while holding a nonzero reader_counters entry, min_epoch will stall and reclamation will block. Options: lease reader heartbeats + detect dead nodes and advance min ignoring them after timeout. But that's riskier for correctness.

nora: also memory overhead: retire_list can grow under churn. We need throttling (backpressure) so eviction slows if retire backlog grows. That maps to a circuit-breaker: when retire_list > X, start rejecting demote requests or extend soft-demote windows.

anya: telemetry thoughts: metric for retire_queue_length, time_to_reclaim, reader_hold_histogram, and reclaim_blocked_by_dead_node_count. Add a safety gate to auto-fall back to conservative reuse (longer quiesce) if reclaim backlog exceeds threshold.

tariq: performance: per-read we only do a store to per-core slot with current epoch. That is ~1-2ns on modern cores if colocated. But we must avoid atomic inc/dec on hotpath. Using preallocated per-core counters and store-only enter/leave is nice.

hao: can we combine EBR with lightweight generation tags for cross-checking? Eg EBR prevents free, gen-tag prevents ABA on metadata updates. Double-protection may be overkill but gives defense-in-depth.

nora: yeah, but keep implementation incremental: prototype EBR in-memory path first (no snapshot changes), add a reclaim monitor and backpressure. If that stabilizes, evaluate adding gen-tags later.

tariq: rollout plan: feature-flag `prefix_ebr_reclaim`. Steps:
1) implement reader annotations + reclamation thread behind flag
2) staging run with synthetic long-read workload and high churn for 24h
3) 1% prod canary on `pool-blue-1` for 48h with strict telemetry checks (retire_len < 1000, reclaim_latency < 30s, no UAF asserts)
4) progressively ramp if metrics stay healthy

anya: dev note: add an escape hatch in operator console to force free by ignoring stuck nodes (manual) but default to safe mode. Also add an endpoint that samples current reader counters for debugging.

ops-bot: deploy: canary initiated for service/prefix-cache on pool-blue-1 (flag=prefix_ebr_reclaim).

hao: testing: build a small fuzz harness that randomly pauses readers and kills nodes to ensure reclaim handles node death heuristics. Also simulate large tenant churn to ensure retire_list backpressure triggers correctly.

nora: one more thing: snapshots on disk. EBR is runtime-only; when we persist snapshots we should checkpoint global_epoch into snapshot metadata so restoring nodes don't accidentally think old epochs are current. Simple approach: on snapshot create new snapshot_epoch = global_epoch and mark slots accordingly; on restore treat any slots with del_epoch < snapshot_epoch as reclaimable only after readers in restored cluster advance.

tariq: ok. I'll draft a short RFC comparing EBR vs gen-CAS vs sequencer. If we prefer EBR we need clear operator playbooks.

anya: thanks. Please include perf microbenchmarks for per-read overhead and worst-case retire_queue memory. If EBR shows prolonged GC stalls, we revisit gen-CAS hybrid.

ops-bot: deploy: canary healthchecks completed on pool-blue-1. No UAF alerts so far.
